title: Vijayendra faces protests at Basavakalyan event over opposition to separate religious status for Lingayats

ai.summary: BJP State president B.Y. Vijayendra faced protests at Basavakalyan event after opposing Lingayats' demand for separate religious status, claiming they are all Hindus.

facts.claim: BJP State president B.Y. Vijayendra was forced to leave the venue midway through his address at the 47th Sharana Kammata and Anubhava Mantapa Utsav in Basavakalyan, Bidar district, on Saturday after his remarks opposing the demand for separate religious status for Lingayats triggered strong protests from Basava followers.
facts.quote: BJP State president B.Y. Vijayendra was forced to leave the venue midway through his address at the 47th Sharana Kammata and Anubhava Mantapa Utsav in Basavakalyan, Bidar district, on Saturday after his remarks opposing the demand for separate religious status for Lingayats triggered strong protests from Basava followers.

facts.claim: The two-day festival was inaugurated by Mr. Vijayendra. Initially, he received applause when he condemned the derogatory remarks made by author Ravi Hanj against Basavanna in his book.
facts.quote: The two-day festival was inaugurated by Mr. Vijayendra. Initially, he received applause when he condemned the derogatory remarks made by author Ravi Hanj against Basavanna in his book.

facts.claim: His remarks provoked strong opposition from sections of the audience. They raised slogans against him, insisting that opposing separate religious status for Lingayats was unacceptable.
facts.quote: His remarks provoked strong opposition from sections of the audience. They raised slogans against him, insisting that opposing separate religious status for Lingayats was unacceptable.

facts.claim: Some protesters also attempted to move towards the dais, leading to commotion and heated exchanges.
facts.quote: Some protesters also attempted to move towards the dais, leading to commotion and heated exchanges.

facts.claim: Basavalinga Pattadevaru, State president of the Lingayat seers’ federation, appealed to the audience not to raise slogans against anyone, pointing out that the organisers themselves had invited Mr. Vijayendra to the event.
facts.quote: Basavalinga Pattadevaru, State president of the Lingayat seers’ federation, appealed to the audience not to raise slogans against anyone, pointing out that the organisers themselves had invited Mr. Vijayendra to the event.

facts.claim: Mr. Vijayendra left the stage following consultations with police officers and other leaders.
facts.quote: Mr. Vijayendra left the stage following consultations with police officers and other leaders.

facts.claim: Ravindra Shabadi, a Lingayat leader associated with the Jagatika Lingayat Mahasabha, justified the protest against Mr. Vijayendra’s remarks. He asserted that Lingayatism was a separate religious entity and not part of Hinduism.
facts.quote: Ravindra Shabadi, a Lingayat leader associated with the Jagatika Lingayat Mahasabha, justified the protest against Mr. Vijayendra’s remarks. He asserted that Lingayatism was a separate religious entity and not part of Hinduism.

ai.background_note: Lingayatism seeks recognition as a separate religion from Hinduism, with the Lingayat seers' federation advocating for this status.
